reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address the key premises. E1 concerns a different W-Ta-Ti-V-Cr system with multi-phase structure and TiC, not equimolar WTaTiVZr, and reports only room-temperature hardness/strength. E2 studies HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr (not WTaTiVZr) at low temperatures (298–573 K), far below the ~1000 °C service condition, and does not compare to pure tungsten or measure plastic strain/toughness. No evidence supports the claimed lattice distortion effects, slip system activation, dynamic recovery, or improved high-temperature ductility/toughness.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a homogeneous BCC solid solution with severe lattice distortion
Severe lattice distortion activates multiple slip systems and enhances dislocation recovery (cross-slip, dynamic rearrangement)
Enhanced dislocation recovery homogenizes plastic deformation and delays crack initiation
This mechanism increases plastic strain and toughness compared to pure tungsten under high-temperature sustained loading
Pure tungsten exhibits limited plasticity and lower toughness due to brittle behavior and high DBTT
